data.narrative:
CORE POWER is a growth-stage nuclear energy company founded by Mikal Bøe that has raised $100M+. The nuclear energy sector comp universe includes 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms, among them Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Stage-progression analysis applies here, using the $100M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for growth-stage advancement, yielding $120M. Peer-median triangulation was inapplicable: while 6 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier valuation yielded fewer than 3 datapoints required for statistical reliability. A sector-wide median would conflate heterogeneous maturity levels and technology approaches, introducing material noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. This range reflects limited methodological triangulation—relying on stage-progression alone—and carries meaningful uncertainty around comparable company selection. Key risks to valuation include technology validation timelines, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity of scaling nuclear infrastructure. The narrow comp set in early-stage fusion and advanced fission reflects sector concentration; broader application across nuclear subsectors may not be reliable.
